'''Alexander Nikolayevich Pechen''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Николаевич Печень}}, born 26 January 1979 in [[Moscow]]) is a Russian physicist and mathematician. In 2009 he became a laureate of the [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists]]<ref name="pechenblav">[http://blavatnikawards.org/honorees/profile/alexander-pechen/ Alexander Pechen, the Blavatnik award winner-2009 (Blavatnik program website)]</ref> (USA), in 2016 was elected to [[Professor of the Russian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="listsofprofs">{{cite web |url=http://ras.ru/about/awards/professorofras/list.aspx |title= Постановления Президиума РАН о присвоении звания "Профессор РАН" (№ 13) [Decisions of the Presidium of the Academy on awarding the title "Professor of the Russian Academy of Sciences"]|language=ru}}</ref> among about 500 top Russian researchers aged under fifty.

== Professional career ==
Pechen studied physics at the [[MSU Faculty of Physics|Faculty of Physics of Moscow State University]], specializing in [[theoretical physics]] and graduating with honors in 2001. He received his PhD ([[Candidate of Sciences|Cand. Sci.]]) in 2004 and [[Doktor nauk]] degree in 2014. Pechen is known for the research in quantum mechanics, [[quantum control]], statistical mechanics, [[open quantum system]]s and [[mathematical physics]].

From 2000 to 2003, Pechen stayed as a visiting researcher at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]]. From 2005 to 2010 he was with Chemistry Department of [[Princeton University]]. It is the work at Princeton that brought him the Blavatnik award; the work has discovered that it is possible to develop a single, unified mathematical treatment for a wide range of open system control phenomena.<ref name="NYASMagazine">{{cite journal |last1= Jeffries |first1= Abigail |date= 17 October 2009 |title= Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists. Meet the 12 finalists in the 2009 competition |url=https://www.nyas.org/magazines/autumn-2009/blavatnik-awards-for-young-scientists/ |journal= The New York Academy of Sciences Magazine}}</ref> The control of open quantum systems is highly important for applications since real controlled atoms and molecules almost always significantly interact with their environment.<ref name="pechenblav"/>

From 2011 to 2013, as a [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions|Marie Curie Incoming International Fellowship]] recipient (ACOLA project), he was working at the Department of Chemical Physics in [[Weizmann Institute of Science|Weitzmann Institute]] in Israel.<ref name="mariecurie">{{cite web |url= https://cordis.europa.eu/project/rcn/98605/factsheet/en |title= Analysis of Controllability and Control Landscapes for Quantum Systems |publisher= Official website of [[Framework Programmes for Research and Technological Development#Framework Programme 7|Seventh Framework Programme]] }}</ref><ref name="pechenblav"/> His work was concentrated on the analysis of quantum control landscapes and, jointly with D.J. Tannor<ref name="prl2011">{{cite journal |last1= Pechen |first1= Alexander |last2= Tannor|first2= David|date= 2011|title=Are there traps in quantum control landscapes? |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |volume= 106 |issue= 12 |article-number= 120402|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.106.120402|pmid= 21517285 |arxiv= 1508.05434|bibcode= 2011PhRvL.106l0402P |s2cid= 44559331 }}</ref> drawing a distinction between kinematic and dynamic critical points he demonstrated the existence of trapping behaviour for quantum control systems.<ref name="science2011">{{cite journal |last1= Yeston |first1= Jake |date= 29 April 2011|title= Look Out for Traps |journal= [[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume= 332 |issue= 6029 |page= 515 |doi= 10.1126/science.332.6029.515-b |bibcode= 2011Sci...332..515Y |doi-access=  }}</ref>

His present affiliations are with the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] (from 2016 to 2019, he headed the Laboratory of Mathematical Methods for Quantum Technologies there, which in 2019 grew up in the Department of Mathematical Methods for Quantum Technologies under his leadership)<ref name="pechenlab">[http://www.mi.ras.ru/index.php?c=show_dep&l=1&id=51 Department at the Steklov Institute headed by A. Pechen (website)]</ref> and [[National University of Science and Technology MISIS|National University of Science and Technology MISiS]], both located in Moscow. In 2013–2016, he served as Academic Secretary of the Steklov Institute.  He is also a member of the Academic Councils of Steklov Institute<ref name="CouncilMIAN">{{cite web |url= http://www.mi-ras.ru/index.php?c=uch&l=1 |title= Academic Council of Stekov Mathematical Institute |publisher= Official website of Steklov Institute |access-date= 2019-05-20 |language=en }}</ref> and MISiS.<ref name="CouncilMISiS">{{cite web |url= https://misis.ru/university/struktura-universiteta/uchenyy-sovet/sostav/ |title= Academic Council of MISiS |publisher= Official website of MISiS |access-date= 2019-05-20 |language=ru }}</ref>

Since 2014, Pechen is a member of the Coordination Council of the Federal Fundamental Scientific Research Programme for 2013–2020 in Russia.<ref name="coordinat">{{cite web |url= http://government.ru/docs/all/93537/ |title= Order of the Government of the Russian Federation (Nov. 3, 2014, № 2185-р) |publisher= government.ru |date= 2014-11-03 |access-date= 2018-10-08 |language=ru }}</ref> In 2014–2018 he acted as coordinator of the research project «Contemporary Mathematics and its applications» (about 120 participants) in Stekov Institute sponsored by the Russian Science Foundation.<ref>See [http://www.mathnet.ru/php/conference.phtml?option_lang=eng&eventID=1&confid=1484 videos from the conference] «Contemporary Mathematics and its applications» dedicated to the results of research supported by the Russian Science Foundation (Nov. 19, 2018).</ref>

Since 2015, he also serves as Academic Secretary of the National Committee of Mathematicians of Russia.<ref name="NKM">{{cite web |url= http://math.ras.ru/en/committee.html |title= National Committee of Mathematicians of Russia |publisher= Official website of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] |access-date= 2019-05-17 |archive-date= 2019-07-15 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190715004230/http://math.ras.ru/en/committee.html }}</ref> He was a member, jointly with [[Arkady Dvorkovich]], [[Sergey Kislyakov]], [[Andrei Okounkov]], [[Stanislav Smirnov]], and [[Victor Anatolyevich Vassiliev|Victor Vassiliev]], of the Russian delegation on the General Assembly of the [[International Mathematical Union]] 2018 in [[São Paulo]], Brazil.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Pechen |first1= Alexander |date= 2018|title= International Congress of Mathematicians 2018: from Rio de Janeiro to St. Petersburg |doi=10.1070/RM9865|journal= [[Russian Mathematical Surveys]]|volume= 73 |issue= 6|pages= 1145–1153|bibcode= 2018RuMaS..73.1145P |s2cid= 127543944 }}</ref> The delegation presented a bid to have the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2022 in [[Saint Petersburg]]. The bid was supported by the Assembly. Now Alexander Pechen is a member of the Organizing Committee of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2022 in Saint Petersburg.<ref name="CommitteeICM2022">{{cite web |url= http://government.ru/docs/35700/ |title= Order of the Government of the Russian Federation (Feb. 9, 2019, № 183-р) |publisher= government.ru. |language=ru|date= 2019-02-09 }}</ref>

== Representative publications ==
* K. A. Lyakhov, H. J. Lee, A. N. Pechen, Some issues of industrial scale boron isotopes separation by the laser assisted retarded condensation (SILARC) method, ''Sep. Purif. Technol.'', 176:4 (2017), 402–411.
* A. N. Pechen, D. J. Tannor, Are there traps in quantum control landscapes?, ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'', 106 (2011), 120402.
* A. Pechen, H. Rabitz, Teaching the environment to control quantum systems, ''Phys. Rev. A'', 73 (2006), 062102. 
* A. Pechen, N. Il'in, F. Shuang, H. Rabitz, Quantum control by von Neumann measurements, ''Phys. Rev. A'', 74 (2006), 052102.
